01 · Why UGC
Why creator videos work
Authenticity
People trust people
A homepage saying "it teaches you any tool" is a claim. A student on their own Mac, unstuck at 1am, is proof.
Show, do not tell
The product is the moment it points
HeyClicky draws on the screen to show where to click. Ten seconds of that on video explains it better than any line of copy.
Objections
Answer "is it watching me?" out loud
It is the first thing people wonder about an AI that sees the screen. A real person pressing the hotkey on camera, then reading your FAQ, answers it.
Phone to Mac
Watched on a phone, used on a Mac
Most people will see these videos on their phone. Your "send it to me" button already emails the download, so every video can end on it.
Fuel for ads
Your best ads come from creators
The strongest creator videos become your TikTok and Meta ads. We test 8 openings per script, so the budget follows what people actually watch.
Doesn't feel like an ad
Looks like a normal post
Mac tips, study set-ups and editing tutorials are what these creators already post. It is still labelled as an ad, it just does not feel like one.
02 · What we learned
Where HeyClicky is today
The product
An AI buddy that lives on your Mac. Press the hotkey and it sees what you see, so you can ask anything out loud, and it draws on your screen to point the way. Say "heyclicky agent" and it goes and does the task. Mac only, macOS Sonoma 14.2 or higher.
Shipped lately
  • Clickys: a little team of agents, each with its own name, memory and job (12 Sep)
  • Invite links at heyclicky.com/@username (24 Sep)
  • Several accounts per app, like a work and a personal Gmail (2 Oct)
  • 36 releases in your changelog since 27 April
Your own channels
@heyclicky on X: 15,393 followers, posting most weeks in the buddy's own voice, with posts at 145K and 118K views. Farza: 129,043 followers on X. Your YC launch says HeyClicky went super viral on Instagram.
Already in motion
  • 25,000+ users on your homepage, and 1.2 million messages by week 20.
  • Farza posted on 27 August that you passed 1,000 paying customers.
  • Greg Brockman and Lenny Rachitsky on your homepage, with Lenny calling it "my new favorite onboarding experience".
What that tells us
The demo travels on its own: Farza's posts reach millions. What is missing is volume: many people, not just the founder and the buddy, showing HeyClicky on their own Macs every week on TikTok and Reels.
The timing
Farza teased a new drop on 23 October, and December finals are close. Something new to show, and students under pressure, give creators a reason to post right away.
Sources: heyclicky.com (homepage, FAQ, changelog, careers and referral terms), the YC company and launch pages, and the X profiles and posts of @heyclicky and @FarzaTV, all read 23 Oct 2026.
03 · The category
What screen-aware AI looks like on TikTok
OpenAI Codex
News travels when it is shown
A creator explaining Codex watching your screen to learn repetitive tasks did 302.3K plays (Matt Wolfe, 23 June). Screen-aware AI gets attention when someone shows it on a real screen.
Google
The cursor is the new home
Google's Magic Pointer was covered as "turns your cursor into an AI agent that sees your screen" in a 31.2K-play post (4 July). The idea you launched in April is now a category.
Wispr Flow
Dictation works with creators
The dictation app your changelog benchmarks against works with creators: Ali Abdaal's post carries a wisprflow.ai/ali link (50K plays, 29 January).
Mac tips and app lists
Where Mac brands pay creators
Labelled paid Mac posts reach millions: 2.5M and 997.5K for @mike.banh, 1.4M for @_chrisasante. Brands already buy this slot.
Also in play
Superwhisper on the dictation side, and "AI that sees your screen" explainers from AI news creators, most of them about the big labs.
The opening for HeyClicky
In the posts we read, the big Mac videos are app lists and the screen-aware AI videos are news clips. Nobody is showing a friendly buddy that teaches you the tool you are stuck in, on a real person's Mac. That lane is open.
Sources: TikTok video pages (plays and paid labels read 23 Oct 2026), heyclicky.com/changelog, and the creators' public profiles.
04 · The objection
Is it watching me? The objection to win
Everyone's first question about an AI that sees the screen is "is it watching me?". Your FAQ already answers it. The answer belongs in the videos too.
What your FAQ says
  • "we never look at your screen unless you press the hotkey."
  • "screenshots are never stored."
  • "we do keep basic text summaries so heyclicky has context."
  • "you can delete your account and all its data in settings."
How the videos answer it
  • Show the key: every script presses the hotkey on camera before HeyClicky looks.
  • Say it plainly: Script C reads the FAQ out loud, word for word.
  • Keep it real: creators only ever show their own screen.
The second question
"Will it work with my apps?"
Your FAQ again: "if you can see it, heyclicky can see it. no plugins or integrations needed." Scripts A and B prove it in a different app every time.
How we use it
The hotkey press is the trust moment. Viewers see that nothing happens until the creator asks, and then they see why it is worth asking.
What creators never say
Nothing beyond the FAQ. No "it keeps nothing" (it keeps basic text summaries), no "100% private", and no features that are not live yet.
Sources: the FAQ on heyclicky.com, read 23 Oct 2026.
05 · Audience
Who to sell to first
Start here
College students on Macs
Stuck in a tool at 1am with nobody awake to ask. You already offer a student discount, and "how I use my Mac for school" posts pull hundreds of thousands of plays. Formats A and D.
Start here
Creatives learning pro tools
Editors, producers and designers in DaVinci Resolve, Logic Pro and After Effects. Your YC launch names them, and HeyClicky draws where to click. Format B.
Broadest reach
New Mac owners and Mac tips fans
The audience for "just got a MacBook?" and "apps you need" lists, the biggest Mac format on TikTok. Formats C and D.
Early adopters
Builders and founders
People who want agents to research, build Mac apps and work across Notion, Gmail and Calendar. Farza's audience, and quick to try new tools. Format C.
Where we would start
Start with students and creatives. They feel the "I'm stuck" moment every week, the drawing on screen is easy to film, and both already watch Mac creators.
06 · The moment
Why the next 10 weeks matter
A new drop this weekend, finals in December, and new Macs opened over the holidays. Each one is a reason to show HeyClicky now.
Now to 1 November
Shortlist approved, creators signed, Pro access set up. The first Script A and D videos go live, built around whatever is new in this weekend's drop.
November
Finals prep. Students film Script A on their real coursework tools, creatives film Script B, and the first hook tests start.
December into January
New Mac season. "Just got a MacBook? Install this first" (Script D) gets the budget, using the hooks that won in November.
What this needs from you
  • Pro access for each creator, so they can film talk and agents freely
  • One short founder clip a month from Farza that creators can stitch
  • A tracked link per creator, like your heyclicky.com/@ invite links, to show which video drove each download
Why not wait for January?
Creator content takes a few weeks to tune. Start now and the proven hooks are ready before the holiday Macs are opened.

Your first four weeks
Week 1 · 26 Oct-1 Nov

Week 4 · 16-22 Nov

Agreement signed and Pro access set up by Friday. First videos live within 14 days of the scripts being signed off.

16 · Ads
How the paid ads would run
1 · Film
Each script is shot once, with 8 different openings.
→
2 · Launch
Each opening runs as its own ad, from the creator's handle as a partnership ad.
→
3 · Read
After a few days we compare cost per download and how many people watch past 3 seconds.
4 · Cut
The weakest openings switch off and the budget moves to the best two.
→
5 · Remix
Winning hooks get new bodies and new creators.
→
6 · Refresh
New creator videos every week, so the ads never go stale.
Where the ads point
heyclicky.com, with one tracking link per creator, so every download traces back to the video that drove it. Viewers on a phone can tap "send it to me" and open the download on their Mac.
Why partnership ads
Ads that run from a creator's own handle look like that creator's post, not a brand ad. That is the format these videos are built for.
What we would need
Access to your TikTok and Meta ad accounts (or we run them from ours), a tracked link per creator, and a weekly look at downloads and new accounts.
17 · Process
How a campaign runs, step by step
1 · Brief
You tell us the goal, the audience and what can and can't be said about HeyClicky.
→
2 · Cast
We shortlist creators by niche, location and median views. You pick.
→
3 · Offer
We send each creator the brief, the dates and the rate.
4 · Sign
A written agreement with every creator, covering usage and disclosure.
→
5 · Scripts
One per format: 8 hooks, a shot list, screens to record and a caption.
→
6 · Film and upload
Creators film on their phones and upload to a private folder only we see.
7 · Review
We check every video within 48 hours. Nothing posts unapproved.
→
8 · Post
On the creator's own account, with the ad disclosure and the paid-partnership label.
→
9 · Pay and report
Creators paid within 7 days of going live. You get a report every Monday.
Where creators talk to us
One hypjam Discord for every creator. Each campaign gets a private channel group for chat, scripts and posted links that only its creators and your team can see.
Access
Each signed creator gets Pro access for the campaign, so they can film talk and agents freely. Nobody shows a feature that is not live yet.
18 · Reporting
What we report, and when
Every video
Views, how many people stay past 3 seconds, average watch time, saves, shares and comments.
Every creator link
A tracking link for each creator, so downloads trace back to the video that drove them.
Every Monday
A short report: every video, the hooks that won, downloads by creator, and what we change next.
Every month
A review call: spend, downloads, cost per result on anything run as an ad, and the plan for next month.
19 · Rules
Rules we never break
Disclosure
"Ad | Paid partnership with HeyClicky" on screen, said in the first seconds, and the platform's paid-partnership label on. That is what the FTC asks for.
Who films
Adults only (18+). Creators use HeyClicky themselves before they talk about it.
What gets said
Nothing your own pages do not say HeyClicky does. No invented numbers. We never pay for a positive opinion, only for the video.
Screens on camera
Creators only record their own Mac, with notifications off and no private messages, emails or other people's data in view.
Students
Every creator we cast is an adult. HeyClicky is shown teaching a tool, never doing graded work, and nobody films in a classroom.
How we run it
Every video reviewed within 48 hours before it posts. Creators paid within 7 days of going live.
